MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  OCTOBER 25, 2016

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:03 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Planning Technician/Code Administrator Jessica Slawson

Others Present:  Jeff Romanelli, Park and Activities Commission
  Victor Yoo, Planning Commission
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineer

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 10, 2016

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 27, 2016
  AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – OCTOBER

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 57506 THROUGH 57553 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $106,746.55 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
OCTOBER 25, 2016
 6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN

  TO APPROVE ITEM A.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to
  the City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be
  read by title only.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

A.  Pam Schachter, 46 Ranchview Road, commented that she represents the
  Ranchview Road Citizens Group consisting of 10 residents who are concerned
  about parking of oversized vehicles on their street. She distributed pictures to the
  COUNCIL illustrating their concerns noting that it has been a difficult situation
  with one particular resident. She further noted that after reviewing the Municipal
  Code, they worked with Planning Director Wahba and Planning Technician/Code
  Administrator Slawson and believed that this individual is not following the spirit
  and intent of the code. Finally, she requested this item be placed on a future
  agenda.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF inquired if any effort was made on the part of the
  residents to communicate with this neighbor. Mrs. Schachter stated that Code
  Administrator Slawson has been out numerous times.

  Mahesh “Mike” Mahajan, 12 Golden Spar, commented that he believes the
  Sheriff’s Department is not enforcing the parking restrictions. He further noted
  his frustration with this bus being allowed to park on the street.

  After brief discussion, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN requested this matter be placed on a
  future agenda and those residents affected will be noticed when that meeting is
  scheduled.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

  NONE

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF OCTOBER 17, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF OCTOBER 17, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  PARK AND ACTVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF
  OCTOBER 17, 2016 – PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council enter into an agreement (on a form
  satisfactory to the City Attorney) with Dave Bang Associates to furnish and
  install the play equipment selected by the subcommittee, including two park
  benches and engineered wood fiber footing material, at the designated new
  location in Ernie Howlett Park at a cost not to exceed $126,700.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 25, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN HUFF inquired if a cost comparison was undertaken.
  Community Services Director Clark explained that all three firms were given a
  budget maximum of $150,000.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL thanked the Park and Activities Commission and
  subcommittee for their work on this project.

  Eric Huber, Vice President, David Bang Associates, explained the process and
  materials that will be used for the playground equipment.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, Mr. Huber noted that the wood
  fiber lasts approximately two years and will need to be topped off and takes about
  seven years before the rubber starts to equal the cost with wood fiber and that
  sand does not last long and is difficult to maintain. He noted that most public
  parks use wood fiber because of the lower cost and between a rubberized surface,
  wood fiber is better.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Mr. Huber noted that the materials
  used will be all natural products.

  Mr. Huber noted that it was his intent to create a destination park with unique
  equipment with each piece being labeled by age group.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE ENTERING INTO AN AGREEMENT (ON A FORM
  SATISFACTORY TO THE CITY ATTORNEY) WITH DAVE BANG
  ASSOCIATES TO FURNISH AND INSTALL THE PLAY EQUIPMENT
  SELECTED BY THE SUBCOMMITTEE, INCLUDING TWO PARK
  BENCHES AND ENGINEERED WOOD FIBER FOOTING MATERIAL, AT
  THE DESIGNATED NEW LOCATION IN ERNIE HOWLETT PARK AT A
  COST NOT TO EXCEED $126,700.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ thanked Mr. Huber for his design and that her
  family utilizes this park extensively. She noted that she was pleased that this
  park offers a variety of activities and addresses various demographics of the
  community.

C.  SOCIAL MEDIA POLICY

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt the Social Media Policy.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  Extensive discussion ensued regarding the various features of the City’s website
  and Facebook.

  City Attorney Davis noted that his primary concern was the potential of
  conducting serial meetings over social media such as Facebook which could
  pose a problem if the COUNCIL was to make comments regarding an upcoming
  project.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF asked if a disclaimer should be included in Section J.
  Assistant to the City Manager Davis noted that she will confirm if one has been
  posted on the various websites.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ explained that the City does not have control over
  those websites it does not own and that advertising is based on the user’s
  preferences.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, Assistant to the City Manager
  Davis noted that “without additional comments posted” could be removed from
  Section F.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 25, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL stated that this policy would also refer to
  Commissioners.

  City Attorney Davis reiterated that individual conversations are permitted under
  the Brown Act, but comments could be restricted depending on how the item is
  posted.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis noted that City Attorney Davis will provide
  a memorandum to the COUNCIL and that training will also be available.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO ADOPT THE SOCIAL MEDIA POLICY DELETING "WITHOUT
  ADDITIONAL COMMENTS POSTED“ AS DESIGNATED IN III. GENERAL
  POLICY, SECTION F, AND INCLUDING A DISCLAIMER STATING "THE CITY
  DOES NOT ENDORSE ANY ADVERTISEMENTS“ ON THE CITY’S VARIOUS
  SITES AS AMENDED.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

D.  ANNUAL AUDIT SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the agreement and rates for
  the CPA firm of Macias Gini & O'Connell LLP to perform audit services for the
  Fiscal Year 2015-16, calculate and prepare the new GASB #68 reports, prepare
  the State Controller's Street Report, and prepare the Pepper Tree Foundation's
  tax returns.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per
  agenda material).

  At MAYOR ZUCKERMAN’S request, Administrative Services Director Whitehead
  explained what is involved in the audit process.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE AGREEMENT AND RATES FOR THE CPA FIRM OF
  MACIAS GINI & O'CONNELL LLP TO PERFORM AUDIT SERVICES FOR
  THE FISCAL YEAR 2015-16, CALCULATE AND PREPARE THE NEW
  GASB #68 REPORTS, PREPARE THE STATE CONTROLLER'S STREET
  REPORT, AND PREPARE THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION'S TAX
  RETURNS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

E.  GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEM (GIS) RENEWAL

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the three-year renewal agreement between the City and Digital Maps for a web-
  based Geographic Information System subscription.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per
  agenda material).

  At MAYOR ZUCKERMAN’S request, Administrative Services Director Whitehead
  explained what is involved with the GIS renewal. He noted that when the new
  website comes online, a cost will be determined at that time.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Planning Director Wahba noted that the
  fee may need to be revisited and suggested including this item for discussion at
  the next Policy Development Session.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 25, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE THE THREE-YEAR
  RENEWAL AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY AND DIGITAL MAPS FOR
  A WEB-BASED GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEM SUBSCRIPTION.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF
  APRIL 6, 2016 - PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH EQUESTRIAN CROSSWALK

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve: 1) Installation of equestrian
  crosswalk on Palos Verdes Drive North at 3739-3815 Palos Verdes Drive North
  to include crosswalk markings, warning signs with rectangular rapid flashing
  beacons and in-roadway warning lights; and 2) Installation of a "Turning
  Vehicles Yield to Pedestrians" sign to address pedestrian and equestrian
  concerns at the crosswalk on Palos Verdes Drive North and Crenshaw
  Boulevard.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN asked the audience for a show of hands in support of this
  project. It was noted that everyone raised their hands.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN thanked Traffic Engineer Itagaki for her work on this
  project and that this will provide additional safety on Palos Verdes Drive North
  and Crenshaw Boulevard.

  Jan Ball noted that this safety measure is very much needed as many riders
  use those trails.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN commented that he was pleased to accommodate
  the unincorporated area of the neighborhood in Westfield. He noted that staff
  did a great job in opening the trail along Palos Verdes Drive North and was also
  pleased that a solution was reached for equestrians and pedestrians to cross
  that intersection.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE: 1) INSTALLATION OF EQUESTRIAN CROSSWALK ON
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AT 3739-3815 PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH TO INCLUDE CROSSWALK MARKINGS, WARNING SIGNS WITH
  RECTANGULAR RAPID FLASHING BEACONS AND IN-ROADWAY
  WARNING LIGHTS; AND 2) INSTALLATION OF A "TURNING VEHICLES
  YIELD TO PEDESTRIANS" SIGN TO ADDRESS PEDESTRIAN AND
  EQUESTRIAN CONCERNS AT THE CROSSWALK ON PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE NORTH AND CRENSHAW BOULEVARD.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Assistant City Manager Grammer noted
  that the design of this area and Rolling Hills Road will be bid together for cost
  efficiency and should take place in the spring of next year.

B.  CITY MANAGER AGREEMENT AMENDMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council formally adopt the Tenth Amendment
  to the City Manager's Employment Agreement.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that this amendment is not part of the City
  Manager’s performance evaluation.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 25, 2016
   City Attorney Davis noted that the agreement will be amended and restated and
  brought back to the COUNCIL at a future meeting.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO ADOPT THE TENTH AMENDMENT TO THE CITY MANAGER'S
  EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  NONE

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ reported that she attended Supervisor Knabe’s State
  of the County event which included an overview of his career in anticipation of his
  upcoming retirement.

B.  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL reported that she attended the South Bay Cities
  Council of Governments (SBCCOG) Housing Summit.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that housing is an important issue for
  everyone. He further noted that this item will be carefully reviewed through the
  General Plan update process.

C.  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL announced that the Air Quality Management
  District (AQMD) will host a town hall meeting on Saturday, October 29, 2016 at
  10:00 a.m. located at the Torrance City Hall Council Chambers to discuss the
  Norton Engineering Alkylation Technology Study related to the use of Hydrofluoric
  Acid in refineries.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or
  issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  BEST CITIES FOR SUCCESSFUL AGING MAYOR’S PLEDGE

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign the Best
  Cities for Successful Aging Mayor's Pledge.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  Brief discussion ensued regarding senior services.  COUNCILWOMAN
  MITCHELL was pleased to note that COUNCILWOMAN HUFF is the Executive
  Director of Healthcare and Elder Law Programs Corporation (H.E.L.P.).

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL reported that she attended the Peninsula Village
  event and was very informative.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted to be mindful to include residents of all
  ages.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
OCTOBER 25, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN HUFF noted that the village concept is a national program
  which emphasizes assisting seniors to remain in their homes and involved in
  the community. She further noted that their office has moved to a new location
  on Silver Spur Road.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO SUPPORT MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SIGNING THE BEST CITIES FOR
  SUCCESSFUL AGING PLEDGE AS SPONSORED BY THE MILKEN
  INSTITUTE.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

14.  CLOSED SESSION

  NONE

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:30 p.m. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN formally adjourned the City Council meeting
  to the Joint Park and Activities Commission City Celebration Debriefing meeting
  scheduled for Tuesday, November 1, 2016 at 6:00 p.m.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Greg Grammer
Deputy City Clerk  Assistant City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
OCTOBER 25, 2016
